hypotheses.claim: A stagnation-adaptive rank-power destroy score with scale-normalized multiplicative gates (load, depot-proximity, demand, route-distance) and an iteration-fraction-dependent relatedness gate will beat the current incumbent (dev_24 mean 16.1391, 24/24 wins vs VBS-equal baseline) especially in the weakest regimes flagged by archive feedback — spatial=clustered (-18.1% rel gap), depot_style=eccentric (-19.1%), demand_dist=uniform (-20.0%), size=100 (-20.3%), capacity_level=loose (-21.6%) — because in clustered/eccentric geometries worst-cost removal repeatedly destroys the same peripheral customers while the real gains come from intra-cluster re-partitioning, which only relatedness-guided ruin with stagnation-driven flatter ranking can reach within the ~200 ms effective anytime window.

next_search_advice.direction: Evolve the single open hook `score_ruin_nodes` into a stagnation-adaptive multiplicative-gated rank-power destroy rule: score_i = rank_power(|removal_savings_i| / scale) * gate_load * gate_depot * gate_demand * gate_rdist, where the rank exponent p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio) anneals from a greedy-biased exponent (near 1, exploit) toward a flatter exponent (near 0.4-0.5, diversify) as stagnation_ratio→1, and all gates are normalized by per-instance scale (mean edge length, mean demand, capacity slack) so the rule stays scale-invariant across size 100/200, loose vs tight capacity, and eccentric-depot geometries; prefer spatially-related removal (distance-from-last-removed-node gate) once iteration fraction exceeds ~0.3 so clustered instances get true Shaw-style relatedness ruin rather than scattered worst-cost removal. Exploration axes for the inner EoH loop: (a) exponent schedule shape (linear vs power vs sigmoid in stagnation_ratio), (b) relative weight of depot-proximity vs route-distance gates, (c) whether ruin-set size grows with stagnation (adaptive q) as a multiplicative amplitude on the same score, keeping the deterministic no-RNG tie-break and the O(n) per-iteration cost required to avoid 2000 ms budget exhaustion.
